allow_private_ips.description:
AllowPrivateIPs is the value a create body should carry for this candidate: a
RECOMMENDATION, never an enforcement. True only when the scan verified the
endpoint is the in-cluster Service form for this server's own namespace.

Always rendered, including as false, so "not offered" stays distinguishable
from "no opinion".

It does not constrain writes: the field is caller-supplied on
ConnectorWriteRequest, so an Admin can post it for any endpoint exactly as
they could by hand. What this constrains is only what the scan OFFERS.

The verification rule and the reasoning behind it live in
models.DiscoveredServer.HasInClusterServiceEndpoint. They are deliberately
NOT restated here: swaggo copies this comment verbatim into all three
swagger.json copies and types.gen.ts, and httpserver/docs.go serves the spec
unauthenticated — so anything written here is published to anonymous callers.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is the server's in-cluster URL in its canonical normalized form —
the value a create body must carry verbatim.

existing_connectors.description:
ExistingConnectors are the Connectors on the scanned Gateway that already
hold this endpoint. Empty means "not yet admitted here".

A list rather than an already_added boolean: it names which Connector an
Admin would be editing instead of creating, and it needs no reshaping if a
Connector ever gains parameters and two Connectors on one endpoint become
legitimate. Always an array, never null — see DiscoveredServerListResponse.

group.description:
Group is the MCPGroup the server belongs to, or "" when it is ungrouped.
No omitempty: ungrouped is a normal state, not an absent field, and a key
that appears only sometimes makes every client distinguish two cases that
mean the same thing.

health.description:
Health is the server's phase as the Operator reports it, or "Unknown" when
the Operator has published none yet.

It is NOT a readiness signal, and no field here is. Whether a server is
running is an Operator fact; whether this Org has finished wiring it is
org-local and is answered by ExistingConnectors below. Presenting the
former as readiness would send an Admin to fix configuration that was never
wrong.

name.description: Name is the MCPServer object's name.

namespace.description:
Namespace is the MCPServer object's namespace. Carried alongside Name
because the pair is the provenance reference an admission records, and
because a cluster-wide scan can legitimately return two servers of the
same name in different namespaces.

transport.description: Transport is the protocol a client actually speaks to the server's proxy.

code.description:
Code is the specific machine-readable reason within Type. Optional: a
message-only error omits it.

message.description: Message is the human-readable description, safe to show to the caller.

type.description:
Type is the broad class of the error. Optional: a message-only error
omits it.
